seo.title: PostHog Alternative: OpenPanel vs PostHog
seo.description: OpenPanel vs PostHog: a 3 KB vs 105 KB tracking script, cookie-free by default, simpler self-hosting, and what each costs at 1M and 10M events a month.

hero.heading: OpenPanel vs PostHog
hero.subheading: PostHog is a large developer platform: analytics, feature flags, experiments, surveys, error tracking and a data warehouse. OpenPanel does product and web analytics only, with a much smaller script, no cookies by default and a self-hosted setup you can run on one server.

competitor.name: PostHog
competitor.short_description: Developer platform that bundles product analytics, session replay, feature flags, experiments, surveys and error tracking.

overview.title: When OpenPanel is the better PostHog alternative
paragraphs: If your team uses PostHog to track events, build funnels and retention charts and watch session replays, and never opens feature flags or surveys, you still carry the rest: a larger script, a heavier self-hosted stack and a separate meter for each product.

The script size difference is large. OpenPanel's web script is 3.3 KB gzipped. PostHog's main browser bundle (posthog-js 1.438, dist/array.js) is about 105 KB gzipped when we measured it in October 2026. On a marketing site or a storefront, that is weight your visitors download before anything else runs.

Privacy defaults differ too. PostHog's JavaScript library stores its state in localStorage plus a first-party cookie unless you change persistence. OpenPanel sets no cookies: it identifies anonymous visitors with a daily-rotating salted hash, so you can run it without a consent banner in most setups.

PostHog is the better choice if you want one vendor for analytics, feature flags, A/B experiments with statistics, surveys and error tracking, or if you want to write SQL against your data. OpenPanel has none of those products, and we would rather you know that before you migrate.

summary_comparison.title: OpenPanel or PostHog?
summary_comparison.intro: Both are open source and both run on ClickHouse. The difference is scope: PostHog bundles a dozen products, OpenPanel does analytics.
summary_comparison.one_liner: Pick PostHog for an all-in-one developer platform; pick OpenPanel for product and web analytics with a 3 KB script and one-server self-hosting.
best_for_openpanel: Teams that use PostHog mainly for events, funnels, retention and session replay
Sites where script weight matters: storefronts, landing pages, content sites
Products that want cookie-free analytics without a consent banner
Teams that want to self-host on a single server with Docker Compose
best_for_competitor: Teams that rely on feature flags and A/B experiments with significance testing
Teams that want surveys and error tracking from the same vendor
Analysts who want to query raw data with SQL (HogQL)
Small products that fit inside PostHog's 1M free events a month

feature_comparison.title: Feature comparison
feature_comparison.intro: Where both have a feature, the depth can differ. Notes explain the gaps.

features.name: SQL queries on raw data
features.notes: PostHog has HogQL. OpenPanel has a visual report builder; self-hosters can query their own ClickHouse directly.

features.name: Session replay
features.notes: OpenPanel replay is opt-in, loads as a separate script and has no per-recording meter.

features.name: A/B experiments with significance
features.notes: In OpenPanel you can break any report down by a variant property, but there is no experiment engine or statistics.

features.name: EU cloud hosting
features.notes: OpenPanel Cloud runs in Germany. PostHog offers an EU region.

features.name: Supported self-hosting
features.notes: PostHog's own docs call self-hosted deployments officially unsupported.

pricing.title: Pricing at real volumes
pricing.intro: PostHog is cheaper for small products and roughly the same as OpenPanel at 10M events, if you only count analytics events. The difference is what else gets metered.

openpanel.model: Flat monthly tiers by event volume
openpanel.description: You pick an event volume and pay a flat price: $90/month for 1M events, $350/month for 10M. Session replay, dashboards, users and projects are not metered separately. There is no free cloud plan: you get a 30-day trial, and self-hosting is free with no event limit.

competitor.description: Product analytics is free for the first 1M events a month, then $0.00005 per event up to 2M and $0.0000343 per event from 2M to 15M, so 10M events cost about $324. Session replay, feature flags, surveys and error tracking each have their own free allowance and meter.
competitor.free_tier: 1M analytics events and 5K session replays a month

migration.title: Moving from PostHog to OpenPanel
migration.intro: The tracking APIs map almost one to one. There is no PostHog importer, so plan to run both tools side by side until OpenPanel has enough history.
migration.estimated_time: An afternoon for the SDK swap; a few weeks of parallel tracking to build history

steps.title: Install the OpenPanel SDK next to PostHog
steps.description: Add the web script or the framework SDK with your client ID. Keep PostHog running for now.

steps.title: Map your calls
steps.description: posthog.capture(name, props) becomes op.track(name, props). posthog.identify(id, props) becomes op.identify({ profileId: id, ...props }). posthog.group() becomes op.setGroup().

steps.title: Rebuild the reports you use
steps.description: Recreate your main funnels, retention charts and dashboards in OpenPanel.

steps.title: Compare numbers for two weeks
steps.description: Check that event counts and funnel conversion match between the two tools before you trust the new one.

steps.title: Remove PostHog
steps.description: Drop the PostHog snippet and keep your PostHog project read-only if you still need old data.

sdk_compatibility.notes: Both use named events with properties and an identify call, so most event names can stay as they are.

historical_data.notes: OpenPanel imports from Mixpanel, Amplitude and Umami, not from PostHog. Keep old data in PostHog or export it through their API.

use_cases.title: Where OpenPanel fits better
use_cases.intro: Four situations where the switch pays off.

items.title: You only use PostHog for analytics
items.description: If your PostHog usage is events, funnels, retention and replay, OpenPanel covers it with one price and one script.

items.title: Page weight shows up in your Core Web Vitals
items.description: Replacing a ~105 KB bundle with a 3.3 KB script is one of the cheaper performance wins on a content or commerce site.

items.title: You want analytics without a cookie banner
items.description: OpenPanel stores nothing in the browser by default. PostHog needs a persistence change, and turning persistence off makes every page load a new anonymous user.

items.title: You want to self-host and have support for it
items.description: OpenPanel's self-hosted version is the full product on a three-service Docker Compose stack. PostHog's hobby deploy is unsupported and limited to free-plan features.

faqs.title: Questions about switching from PostHog
faqs.intro: Short answers, with the trade-offs left in.

items.question: Is OpenPanel cheaper than PostHog?
items.answer: Not always. Under 1M events a month PostHog analytics is free and OpenPanel Cloud is not. At 10M events the two are close ($350 vs about $324 for PostHog analytics alone). OpenPanel gets cheaper when you also use session replay heavily, because replay is not metered separately. Self-hosting OpenPanel is free.

items.question: What do I lose if I leave PostHog?
items.answer: Feature flags, A/B experiments with statistics, surveys, error tracking, heatmaps and SQL access. If you use any of those, you need another tool for that part, or PostHog is the better fit.

items.question: Can I import my PostHog data?
items.answer: No. OpenPanel has importers for Mixpanel, Amplitude and Umami. For PostHog, run both tools in parallel for a few weeks and keep the old project for historical questions.

items.question: Does OpenPanel have session replay?
items.answer: Yes. It is opt-in, loads as a separate script only when enabled, and recordings are kept for 30 days.

items.question: How hard is self-hosting compared with PostHog?
items.answer: OpenPanel runs on Docker Compose with ClickHouse, Postgres and Redis, and a setup script configures it. PostHog's hobby deploy adds Kafka, ZooKeeper and MinIO, needs 16 GB of RAM, and PostHog says it is officially unsupported.

items.question: Is OpenPanel open source like PostHog?
items.answer: Yes. The platform is AGPL-3.0 and the SDKs are MIT. PostHog is MIT apart from its ee/ directory. AGPL means that if you modify OpenPanel and offer it as a service, you share those changes.
